utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Good morning to all of you. Good morning, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We left off on Thursday with the document that pertains to Foca. Now, my question to you was whether you overlooked -- or why did you overlook the very essence, the gist of this document, where the authorities are preventing the departure, and a demand is made to actually put a stop to the expulsions and not to expel people, as you claimed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it possible for me to see a copy of that document, because my recollection of it is the opposite, that they are discussing how to organise the departure of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, that's Exhibit P2642.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will we see this document in e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read paragraph 1 as saying that they will allow people to depart. And paragraph 3, they're organising that. Paragraph 4 calls on the police and civilian authorities to organise transportation. And paragraph 5 is to make a list of property that will remain when the people leave. So I see this as an example of a war commission, in this case, acting to organise the departure of Muslims after consulting with the commissioner sent from the government level. I agree that the second paragraph -- third paragraph says that they have, until now, been preventing both Serbs and Muslims from leaving, but the gist of this decision I see as how to organise the departure of those who want to leave, as the letter expresses it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Ms. Hanson, I will have a problem with the way you understand documents, not with documents, themselves. This is a clear suggestion that there was a ban, so these people wanted to go. And now you say that things should be organised for those who wish to go. This is not expulsion. This is about making it possible for people, Serbs and Muslims alike, to leave and to join their families, and you misrepresented that in your report. You painted it in a completely different light; is that so?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, I cite this document as an example of communications with the government commissioner. However, I certainly see here that they are putting it in terms of organising the departure of those who wish to leave. I note that in my report, that one of the criteria that is set in many -- by many crisis staffs for the departure of the non-Serbs is that they sign a paper stating they're leaving voluntarily. I think the overall evidence of the events throughout the municipalities indicate why people would say such a thing, and it is not a truly spontaneous desire to move to a different place. In some cases, they wish to avoid war operations, perhaps. But in other cases, they were forced into such a situation that departure was seen as the only option. In Bosanska Krupa, for example, the Crisis Staff wrote, and those are the words of Gojko Klickovic, member of the Main Staff, that two options were suggested to the Muslims; to organise their own departure or to have it effected by military means. He then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, we'll get to that. Now we're in Foca. We're dealing with Foca now. And in some municipalities, this is not allowed. Do you know, by the way, that Mr. Klickovic, against whom you testified before the court in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that he was acquitted because he did not harm Serbs at all, and that this Court is not in favour of Bosnian Serbs at all? So in this case, you cannot say that they were forced in some municipalities. We have to determine in what municipalities, under what circumstances. And I asked you whether you knew that Mr. Klickovic, before a Court which is very much anti-Serb, that he was acquitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I don't think that question is appropriate for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question is whether she knew that a certain individual was acquitted. I think she mentioned his name in her answer previously. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did bring up his name. I knew he was acquitted, but I can't agree with the entire statement, that the Court is anti-Serb. So how can I answer a question that I agree with half of, but not the other half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please confirm for the Trial Chamber whether Gojko Klickovic was the president of the Crisis Staff in the municipality of Bosanska Krupa that you mentioned? And you mentioned a document that he drafted. Is that the Gojko Klickovic we're talking about, the same person?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 147 of your report, you present some conclusions that pose a great challenge for the Defence, and they are the foundation of the charge in the indictment that the Bosnian Serb leadership did not have any institutional authority over crisis staffs, as members of the Presidency and Government, but that they did everything, they assisted and so on. And then you say: "As the president of the Presidency of Kotor Varos, a municipality that witnessed some of the worst violence quoted ..." [In English] "Indeed as the president of the War Presidency of Kotor Varos Municipality, Kotor Varos, a municipality that witnessed some of the worst violence, put it as far as the action concerning the hand-over of arms and moving people out of the municipality is concerned, the action and all activities in general were carried out on the order of the Government and Presidency of the Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That should be "not only," that did not have only the institutional authority of a crisis staff, but they did everything. Just a second. Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is it possible for me to have a copy of my report when he cites paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means. The last paragraph, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that's Exhibit P2589, and a hard copy of the report is coming down to the courtroom as we speak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like her to get a hard copy, because we're wasting time. While we're waiting for you to get it -- okay, yes. I would really like the witness to be given a hard copy, because we can't waste time waiting for each and every paragraph to be called up on the screen. I think that the witness can then look at the hard copy and everybody else can check their own copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A hard copy is coming. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter document 532.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since, Ms. Hanson, you list Kotor Varos as an example of wrong-doing, now I would like us to look at Kotor Varos and to verify what actually happened there and what your conclusions should have been, and then we will deal with other municipalities. Please look at this document. This is a session of the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos, 25th of June; that is the date. And now look at the first paragraph: "In combat activities in the course of the day, the members of the Crisis Staff were informed about them by Colonel Peulic, and he also informed the crisis staff of a telegram from the corps commander relating to the security for the arrival of Banja Luka Bishop Komarica for a religious service in Kotor Varos to be held on Saturday, and that measures must be taken to make this possible. With regard to the development of events in our area, he ordered that anyone that can carry a rifle must be mobilised. The town command must be formed ..." And so on. Do you know that Bishop Komarica is the local religious leader of Roman Catholic Church and that he is an ethnic Croat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we looking at the correct document, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so. That's the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that Bishop Komarica is the Catholic bishop and a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now look at the end of this paragraph, where it says that Dr. Gajanik informed the Crisis Staff about the condition of the wounded, and he says that they have a total of 10 people dead and 31 wounded. Do you know that throughout this area, there was fighting going on in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware that there was armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Bishop Komarica is coming to visit Croats for their religious holiday, not Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which religious holiday, but he is coming, yes, presumably to minister to Croats or Catholics, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that's at the end of the third month of war. This municipality makes it possible for a bishop of a minority population to come and visit, provides security, and orders that additional forces be mobilised in order to ensure his safety during his visit. Did you have this document when you were making your report, and did you take it into account? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is too complicated to give a yes or no. I don't see that the additional forces mobilised is expressly to ensure his safety. Yes, I reviewed all the minutes of the Crisis Staff -- meetings of the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos, so I would have seen this one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you did not take it into account; is that so?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed it. I did not put it in my report. I did not enter into issues of religious services or -- this bishop is in Banja Luka, which is already part of the Serb-held territory. He's moving between two Serb-held areas. I didn't go into detail into that sort of -- a visit like that. I did not -- I read it. I did not include it in my report. I don't know what you mean, did I take it into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, it's the third month of the war, it's at the end. The Croat minority in Kotor Varos is still there. They have their religious services. The Catholic bishop comes to visit them, and the authorities are trying to make sure that everything goes as it should. And you are insinuating that they are -- they have expelled everyone. You can see clearly here that additional forces are mobilised in order to secure Komarica's visit, but you said that you did not take this document into account. I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you ask a question? Do you like to comment, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The quotation which he started this section with, paragraph 147, as you can see from the footnote, refers to -- is dated from October, not June. We see later, in Kotor Varos, more organised departures in July and August. Of course, there were some non-Serbs left, especially in Banja Luka, in 1992. I don't claim that they got rid of -- they moved out everybody, but they -- this body, the Crisis Staff, is formed to defend Serb interests in territory that contains non-Serbs as well, and a pattern I see throughout is that that brings an inherent conflict when power is wielded in the name of one people in territory that contains Serbs, Croats and Muslims. So this is proof that there are still Croats in Kotor Varos. I agree that their bishop is coming to visit them. But it does not negate the later minutes of the crisis staffs and War Presidency that say, We've got to figure out why not everyone wants to leave, we've got to organise their departure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1294, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will get to that, Ms. Hanson. Can we please look at 65 ter 276.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is two days later, the 27th of June, the meeting of the same body again. And in item 1, it says that Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic informed the staff about combat operations, and it says: "Mane T.," probably Mane Tepic, "reported on the situation in the units securing the town, stressing that during the night, the situation in the units was stable, and the enemy was seen setting fire to Serbian houses in Kotor." And in item 2, at the end, it says: "The Crisis Staff was made aware of the requests of the Red Cross and the request of Naim Hadziselimovic for permission to exchange his house, which was given on the condition that he brings the proper documents as proof of the exchange." Do you know that at that time, Serb houses were being set on fire in Kotor Varos, itself, that there are enemy units present there, and that Naim is a Muslim who is seeking permission to exchange his property?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see all that from the document, I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter 290.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, this is the 29th of June, two days later, another meeting of the Crisis Staff. A shortage of oil is mentioned here, shortage of a number of items, and it says: "At about 2300 hours yesterday, a group went into action in the Rujik area, on which occasion one soldier was killed and another seriously wounded." And: "Kotoriste must be cleaned again because in the course of the day because there are a lot of people there." And then in the last paragraph: "Due to the frequent occurrence of flat break-ins, an order was issued to the tenants' councils in blocks of flats to organise guard duty in their building and to check persons entering and leaving them. The tenants' councils shall be responsible for every unauthorised entry into flats." Are you aware of this, that this was organised, and do you know that this was done in accordance with the law?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the last paragraph of the tenants' councils?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that here. I have no basis to say whether it was or was not in accordance with the law, but I see that it is written here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter 300.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is another session of the War Presidency. The date is the 15th of July, so it's no longer the Crisis Staff, it's the War Presidency. And we can see everything from this document. Look at item 3: "Under this item, the work of the Red Cross was discussed; i.e., the possibility of a visit from a representative of the International Red Cross. It was decided that the Red Cross should become more active in this field of work by visiting prisoners, passing messages from their families to them, and preparing for a visit from an International Red Cross representative." Are you aware of the fact that the International Red Cross was active there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware, in general terms, of the International Red Cross seeking access to many detention centres. The story in Kotor Varos, itself, I'm not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1297.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to look at 65 ter 458, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date is the 8th of August. This is the 51st session, which means that they had a session practically every day. And in item 3, it says: "The Presidency considered the Executive Committee's proposal to grant permission for the operation of a private company, Bosna Kompanija in Siprage ..." And other matters. So they gave their approval for the operation of this company, Bosna Kompanija. And it says: "Savo reported on the unsanitary conditions in the prison." Do you know which ethnicity is in the majority in Siprage?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Siprage has a Muslim majority, and we will have to look at it in the end, show that. It says here: "Savo reported on the unsanitary conditions in the prison." That's the translation that we have of this document and it says Savo presented the problem of unsanitary conditions in the prison, which means that it was a problem which was being solved. So the translation is wrong. And as regards the various places, Siprage, as you will see, is a Muslim village. It has a marked Muslim majority in Kotor Varos. So I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Instead of making a statement, why don't you read the last sentence on item 4 so that we can hear the correct interpretation. And I ask Ms. Hanson to read out that sentence, starting out with "Savo."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Savo raised the problem of unsanitary conditions in the prison."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 295, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session, the 57th session, on the 21st of August, 1992. In fact, it's the 59th meeting. We see the agenda, and the second paragraph: "Pursuant to the information reported, President Djekanovic pointed out matters and problems that needed to be solved to prevent pressures and provocations by certain members of the Special Forces unit directed against Muslim and Croat families in order to compel them to leave should be stopped; that the question of what to do with several families from Gornji Cepak who cannot stay there, but are still in Cepak, should be dealt with, and that the killing of the Orsulic couple should be investigated." Item 4 in English, we need the next page. The translation says "should be," and the proper translation should be "would be" or "to be." Item 4: "Under this item of the agenda, the case of Mirso Alen Avdic was considered, and the recommendation that he be issued documents to travel abroad and visit his father. Problems were discussed and security arranged for a convoy of people wishing to leave the area, scheduled for next Sunday." My first question: Do you see that in this paragraph 2, there is talk about pressures and problems created by certain individuals, and the authorities require action to be taken?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not individuals; it's a unit. Oh, individuals from a unit of special units. Yes, they are describing that there have been unacceptable pressures put on Muslims and Croats to move out, and that should be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, do you agree, concerning item 4, that this Mirso Alen Avdic is a Muslim, and his departure to a destination abroad is being approved?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name certainly suggests a Muslim, and, yes, his departure is being approved by the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 436, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the 12th session of the War Presidency. The Crisis Staff is long gone. It's the 13th of July, 1992. Look at item 1: "Mane Tepic ..." [In English] "Mane Tepic informed members of the War Presidency about yesterday's events on the ground. At the president's proposal concerning the initiative and wishes of a group of Vecici inhabitants who want to move out, it was concluded that efforts should be made to make it possible." [Interpretation] Did you know that Vecici had a large Muslim concentration and a large armed group that was constantly involved in combat?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know the specifics of the population or events in Vecici, but I'm not surprised, reading this, to learn that it's non-Serbs who want to move out. I said that I see many documents in which the War Presidency is assisting the moving out of people who say they want to move out. I don't see them anywhere saying, Let's try and make these people want to stay, let's change conditions that would change the mind of all our population and make them want to stay in their home territory. That's what I don't see in any crisis staff or War Presidency minutes, of wanting to find out why they want to leave and changing that. On the contrary, I find in Kotor Varos, itself, a document saying some people who were supposed to leave haven't and the reasons for that should be looked at. And it's given as an example of a poorly-organised departure. So I agree, this is an example of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, Ms. Hanson, we'll come to that, we'll come to that. I don't need your moral position on this. This is a criminal case. You knew that Vecici had a large Muslim concentration and a very strong armed group that was constantly involved in fighting; did you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Ms. Hanson: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think it's proper for the accused to say, I don't need your moral position on this, this is a criminal case, when Ms. Hanson is simply answering the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Yes, Ms. Hanson, could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I already did further up that I didn't know the specifics of the population or events in Vecici.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 274, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, with all due respect, let us stick to questions. There are many documents concerning this municipality which you singled out as representative. We'll go through everything. Everything will fall into its proper place. Please stick to questions. This is the 15th session of the War Presidency, held on 14 July. Item 2, one paragraph before last: "Regarding the pronounced problem of providing accommodation for families from Kotor whose houses had been burnt down by extremists, a temporary solution needs to be found and the Presidency informed." We saw, in 65 ter 276, that Serb houses were ablaze, were being burnt in Kotor Varos, itself, that extremists were all over the place. Did you see that in the previous document, 276?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that extremists were all over the place, but we saw it said that some Serb houses in Kotor were being burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 3: "Under this item, the meeting reviewed the issue of houses remaining vacant after evacuation, and in some recent cases, people have moved into them. It was decided that the competent commission should seal all such houses and submit a list to the Public Security Station." Did you know that municipal authorities, in the middle of this chaos, still found the time to look after property, vacant property?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see is crisis staffs, war presidencies, taking over this vacant property and reassigning it, reusing it in some cases. Here, it seems to be preventing people who have moved in on their own, but that the authorities are trying to assert control over that property. That's what I -- how I read item 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, please, let's discuss only Kotor Varos now, because you cited it in your last paragraph of the report as representative. Let's concentrate on that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we not? We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 550, please. 65 ter 550.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session of 18 June. The Crisis Staff is still there, and it says, towards the end of the second paragraph: "Goran Krsic informed the Crisis Staff that there were two requests to return into abandoned apartments." Next page in English. "Goran Krsic informed the Crisis Staff that there were two requests to return into sealed apartments." Two Muslim names are quoted: "Huseinovic was given permission to move back into his flat, but not Ibricic, since he was not the tenancy right holder. The Crisis Staff was informed of the activities of the Municipal Civilian Protection Staff." These two persons, Huseinovic and Ibricic, were they Muslims, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names are certainly Muslim, so the assumption is they identified themselves as Muslims, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you register that on the 18th of June, Muslims were returning to their apartments in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not put this in my report, if that's what you mean by "registering."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you, as an unbiased expert, have the obligation to include exculpatory elements into your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Exculpatory" I take to mean that crimes did not occur or that someone else, other than the accused, would be responsible for the crimes. For a crisis staff to allow a citizen to return to his apartment does not strike me as, in itself, exculpatory. It's what I would expect a municipal government to do. I note that item 2 in here is quite consistent with what I say about the people -- non-Serbs can move out if they give up their apartment. That's what we see in item 2. I don't see the fact that one Muslim is allowed to enter his own apartment as exculpatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you are accusing this Crisis Staff that, under the leadership of the Presidency and Government of Republika Srpska, it was persecuting Muslims consistently. This is evidence that it was not so. Chaos reigned in the town. There was fighting and shooting everywhere around, and still, under those circumstances, this War Presidency acted as a responsible government. You did not stress that. On the contrary, you left us with the impression, in paragraph 147, that it was quite the contrary. Can we see the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are making statements without asking a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, did you accuse this Crisis Staff, in your report, about the expulsion of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have difficulty with the word "accused." I stated what I saw it doing. I nowhere said that they expelled every single last non-Serb. As we saw from the document we looked at last week, they wanted to remove non-Serbs to a level at which Serbian power could be assured in the territories they claimed. But as for the accusations, that's not my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said earlier today -- you say they did not expel everyone, but show us one person whom they did expel? Did they expel this person from item 2, Mehmedovic, Rasim, who is asking permission to move out on the condition that he leaves behind his apartment in Kotor Varos? Do you know what occupancy right means under our legislation, that the apartment belongs to the municipality, but it is being used by the person to whom it was allocated?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm satisfy with the [indiscernible] occupancy right. The apartment can belong to the municipality or his place of employment. And, yes, he has the right to occupy it temporarily, although -- not temporarily. He is given the right to occupy, but it is not out-and-out possession.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question asked before that question was whether you can show us one person whom they did expel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this document, no, if that's the question relating to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of paragraph 2 under item 1, you see it says: "The decision was taken that the order to gather foodstuffs be extended to the Siprage co-operative, and the distribution be done from that shop, and that work obligation be introduced in Siprage, Grabovica ..." And another place. Does this concern produce to be distributed among the population?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just reading the B/C/S because I do not see the English yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In English, it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that sentence, yes. What was your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the same place, Siprage, where Muslims were an overwhelming majority?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It mentions Siprage as the name of an economic enterprise here, probably found in the settlement of Siprage, but I don't know for sure. And as I say, I don't know that Siprage has an overwhelming Muslim majority --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see item 1: "Agricultural cooperative Zadruga from Vrbanjci (systemisation was conditionally accepted)." Do you know that this place, Vrbanjci, was almost purely Croat? Just yes or no? Did you know that Vrbanjci is a purely Croat village?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says after this item 4: "The president of the Crisis Staff informed the staff that there are strong pressures and requests by individuals to leave Kotor Varos. After debate, it was agreed that those who live near the front-line and wanted to be evacuated within the municipality should be enabled to do so." Do you know that it's the obligation and the right of municipal authorities to evacuate people who may be jeopardised?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would expect municipal authority to evacuate people in danger. These are to be evacuated within the area of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1302, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 367, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, as we look for that document, can you assist me? In paragraph 147: "Indeed, as the president of the War Presidency of Kotor Varos, a municipality that witnessed some of the worst violence ..." When you say "violence," what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fighting, killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: War?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More than that. Not equal combat, but also civilians, non-combatants detained, put in their -- detained in horrible conditions, maltreated there, and then forced to leave because of the threat of violence or actual killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we will stick to Kotor Varos and show all documents that are available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session from the 15th of July, 1992. Look at item 2, the penultimate paragraph: "The president of the War Presidency stressed that the Presidency had already noted more than once that the situation was taking a bad turn and that the Presidency was ready to do its best -- to do everything in its power to change this. He mentioned, as evidence of this bad situation, that several Serbian families were spending nights in other people's houses, that is to say, outside their homes, than either Muslims or Croats." Did you know that more Serbs were spending nights in other people's houses than Muslims and Croats, and that Serbs were at a greater risk than Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that the War Presidency sees that as a criteria and that the situation is bad. If more Serbs are not securing their homes than Muslims or Croats, that's when the Presidency feels they should change it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1303, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who forced these Serbs to spend nights outside their homes? Was it the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you conclude. You make conclusions. You are very creative in your conclusions. If Croats and Muslims feel safer in their homes than Serbs, then who is perpetrating crimes there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would take this to be general combat activities. There's certainly not enough to say that Muslim or Croat forces are targeting Serbs here. We don't know. It's ... We see in the previous paragraph that 70 per cent of all soldiers who have been killed have lost their lives outside combat, so there's some violence going on, but there's no indication here of it being -- of Muslims or Croats directing fire or arms at Serb families. "Fire" in the sense of shooting, not setting on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your conclusions are very valuable to me. We'll leave them for later. Can we see 65 ter 314.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session from 18 July. Item 1: "The decision was made that due to shortage of manpower in the active-duty police force, the reserve police force should be built up. In that way, the lack of active-duty policemen --" Next page in English, please: "In that way, the shortage of active-duty police officers would be offset by the increased reserve police forces, while the size of the reserve force should be decreased by manning active-duty police. Regarding requests by families whose houses had burnt down to be given accommodation, it was decided that they should all submit a request to the municipal Civilian Protection Staff, which staff will address their accommodation." Do you see that this refers to all families, regardless of faith and ethnic background, and that there was not enough housing?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that in this reference here, they do not specify any ethnic background of the families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at the continuation of this document, where it says that a decision was made to carry out the harvest on all plots where owners are absent, and that all the crops should be taken in by the co-operative, with proper records being kept. So did you notice here that care is taken of the property belonging to owners that are absent, and that records are kept of all the crops harvested from their plots of land?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly here that they will harvest all available crops. The precise record-keeping doesn't mean that's going to be -- the owners are going to be reimbursed or anything. But, naturally, there the War Presidency is trying to, you know, take care of the resources of the municipality, including food. That doesn't surprise me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if proper records are being kept, well, does it say here that they will not be paid? Why are they keeping records, if not for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps to avoid black market -- you know, diversion of the resources out of the control of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And do you see item 3, where it says: "At the request of Spasen Topic --" "Next page in English language: "So regarding Spasen Topic's request for authorisation to go to Belgrade in order to sort out his pension, the War Presidency decided to authorise Topic -- Topic's departure to Belgrade." To you knowledge, would this Spasen Topic be a Serb, based on his name?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name would suggest Serb to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that Serbs needed authorisation to leave the territory of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, if he's of military age. Does it suggest -- when it says he would be engaged in an adequate position in the brigade, it's very clear that the municipal authorities were very sure to keep men of -- Serbs of military age engaged and would not let them go abroad without permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is a retired person, he is retired, because -- well, do you see these things that you are saying anywhere in this document, and don't you see that this is a retired person?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: A retired person who, upon his return, is to be engaged in the brigade. You can retire at an age where you're still fit for military duty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be received, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter 402.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session of the War Presidency of the 23rd of July, 1992. Please look at item 2, the penultimate paragraph: "The Commission for Abandoned Flats and Houses was given the task of checking if all abandoned flats and houses had been sealed ..." Next page in the English language, please. So: "... if all abandoned flats --" My apologies. Can we please go back to the previous page in the English language. So that would be item 2. So: "... if all abandoned flats and houses had been sealed and if there had been instances of people moving in." And now we can go on to the next page in the English language. And we can see from this that the commander asked for permission for a fighter in his unit, Ostoja Popovic, to be authorised to travel to Italy on business, and it says here: "No decision was taken in respect of this request." So were you aware of the fact that abandoned flats and houses were sealed, that the municipal authorities were taking good care of the abandoned property?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see that they're sealed. We also see them receiving applications for people to get some shelter, those whose houses have been destroyed. The level of care taken of them can't be judged, but here the municipality is sealing and controlling those houses. Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be received, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to look at 65 ter 273.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the session of the 24th of July, again the same War Presidency. It says down there that Ljubo Gavric is to compile and forward to the Presidency a detailed report on the resettlement of the population, including the following data: the number of convoys moved out so far; the number of persons who have moved out and the structure of the people who moved out; who carried out the transportation, in which conditions; a financial report with updated information on receipts and expenditures and other relevant information." Do you agree with me that this is the Presidency of Kotor Varos and that it should provide this information to the presidency of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the last question. Perhaps there was a problem with the translation, this is the presidency -- that it should provide the information to the presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that Mr. Ljuboje Gavric should compile and forward to the Presidency the report. What Presidency?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Presidency of Kotor Varos, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last item in the Serbian version - we can go on to the next page in the English version: "Goran Krsic is to be relieved of all tasks related to the harvest to devote his attention to making an inventory of abandoned houses, apartments and other property and their conservation." Now I would like us to go to the next page in the Serbian version: "... that special care be taken of protecting the property in the houses from which entire families had moved out, and that daily reports should be submitted to the War Presidency on all activities regarding the sealing of such property. "Regarding the problems regarding property exchanges, we must prepare decisions enabling tax-free property exchanges and a decision preventing fictitious exchanging and profiteering." Were you aware of the fact that the municipal authorities in Kotor Varos were trying to protect the abandoned property and to deal with the issue of exchanges of property with appropriate regulations in order to prevent looting and profiteering?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The property exchanges commissions or agencies we see set up all over the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, Madam, we're now talking about Kotor Varos. Please, Kotor Varos. You listed this municipality as an example, a representative example.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a municipality where people could bring only 300 Deutschmarks with them when they left, so they left behind quite a bit of property, I imagine. And, yes, here the War Presidency is sealing and holding that property, and setting up or dealing with the property -- the problems of property exchanges.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter 17271.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any law regulating the possession of cash in Yugoslavia, foreign currency in cash or is it something that the authorities in Kotor Varos thought up?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They got it from the ARK, the regulation of not taking out more than 300 marks. As for the legal situation in the former Yugoslavia, I'm not familiar with it. But Deutschmarks were generally used as the default currency because the dinar was going into inflation in the war situation. People didn't know which dinar to use, so Deutschmark was essentially the -- was another currency in use. I know that the instructions on 300 Deutschmarks came from the ARK, and Kotor Varos received and implemented it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at this document. The date is the 31st of July, 1992, and it says that the public security stations in the Banja Luka centre area. It's addressed to all of the police stations in that area: "Recently, under the auspices of the Red Cross, the Caritas and the Bureau for Resettlement of the Population, people are moving out to Croatia, Slovenia and other countries in Western Europe, a large number of people of the Croat and Muslim ethnicity, and it has come to our attention that those people are taking out of the Autonomous Region of Krajina large quantities of foreign currency in order to be able to take unified positions. We hereby issue the following instructions to be complied with when convoys are leaving the area:" So natural persons leaving the area of Autonomous Region of Krajina can take with them a maximum of 300 German marks or the equivalent amount in other currency. And taking into consideration the vagueness of the term "leaving," the SFRY Law on Foreign Exchange was consulted. The law adopted by the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina until the new law was passed. Article 80 of the law states: "Citizens can take abroad only the foreign currency withdrawn from their foreign currency accounts." Please, can we move on to the next page in the English language. "... foreign currency savings deposits, as well as foreign currency bought from authorised banks in keeping with the regulations." It is also stated in the quote that: "The limit of the amount of foreign currency that might be taken abroad is determined by Federal Executive board. Consequently, the decision of the ARK Crisis Staff, published in the ARK Official Gazette number 2 from the 5th of June, 1992, is not in contrast to the valid law on Foreign Currency. Therefore, the following actions are to be taken while inspecting the above-mentioned natural persons:" And let us move on: "Each natural person leaving the ARK, trying to take with them a larger amount of foreign currency than allowed by the appropriate provisions, shall be seized, with the appropriate receipt being issued to them. This money shall be deposited in the safe of the Public Security Station, and natural persons in possession of appropriate authorisations from the authorised banks in the ARK, in accordance with appropriate law, may take with them amounts greater than 300 German marks."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic is kindly asked to read more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't say in the transcript "temporarily seized ."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 100 of your report, you say the Crisis Staff -- I will read in English: [In English] "... the Crisis Staff oversaw the removal of non-Serbs from the municipalities by establishing committees for emigration, travel agencies and the exchange agencies." [Interpretation] And in 101, you say: [In English] "... a maximum sum of money, usually 300 Deutschmarks that deportees could take with them." [Interpretation] So are you giving the full information to the Trial Chamber regarding the rights that people had to take foreign currency with them?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document you provide confirms my assertion. It gives more detail, but it confirms that the ARK decided it and it was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, did you inform the Trial Chamber in your report that this sphere was regulated by the federal law, adopted by Republika Srpska, and that the 300 German marks limit pertained only to the money that had not been withdrawn in accordance with the regulations from one's bank account or purchased in a bank or a foreign exchange office, that the excess amounts were seized temporarily, and that if you were in a position of appropriate authorisations, you could take more money with you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't see the part where you said that it was -- the 300 was only over and above what people had taken out of their ... I guess you mean the fourth item: "Natural persons with valid certificates from authorised banks are allowed to take out more than 300 marks." Is that what you mean by the "over and above"? But the federal law you cite makes no mention of this 300 as a limit. And as for it being a temporary confiscation, I don't see any convincing evidence that these crisis staffs intended people to move out temporarily and made any effort to return them when the situation was more peaceful. It was not -- this removal was not simply for the duration of the war. It was to change the make-up of the municipalities. So to say it's a temporary confiscation of funds is not exactly honest here, because the intention was that these people leave forever. But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, Ms. Hanson, it's not up to you to decide that, it's the Trial Chamber's job, and you're trying to take it upon yourself to do it. So this document that provides the legal basis for the seizure of foreign exchange currency above a certain limit, did you include this in your report? Did you specify that this was in line with the federal law and that seizure of this unlawful foreign currency is only temporary? Did you put this in your report or not? And leave the adjudication to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not, as I see, simply a matter of adjudication. It's the Kotor Varos Crisis Staff or War Presidency later saying, We will decide who can return and who cannot. So that's the basis on which I talk about Kotor Varos saying they didn't expect everyone to come back. As for -- Obviously, no, I did not include this document or any reference to federal laws on currency controls in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned foreign currency, because in paragraph 101 of your report, you say that restrictions were in place and that foreign currency was confiscated. So how can you say that you never mentioned it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must be a mistake in translation. I said I make no reference to federal regulations on currency controls.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are sitting on a regular schedule today, until 1.45. It's time to take a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the Trial Chamber to consider this issue: I would like to remind you that Donia and Treanor have not been examined. I would like to ask you to give me enough time to examine this witness, because these are the fundamentals on which the indictment is based. And this is Prosecution examination, and they took twice as much time as they had previously indicated, and I would like to get twice as much time as I was initially allocated, which is still below what I had asked initially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You still have a long way to go. We'll have a break for 20 minutes and resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. While we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: While we're getting settled, if I can just take a minute to withdraw our fourth motion for binding order against the Government of Bosnia which was filed on the 7th of June. And since then, we've received the materials that we had asked for. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We had expected that. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, in paragraph 100 of your report, you say -- well, we've read it already. You say: [In English] "The Crisis Staffs oversaw the removal of non-Serbs from the municipalities by establishing 'committees for emigration,' 'travel agencies' and 'exchange agencies'." [Interpretation] Let us now address this through 65 ter 1067. Here, at the top, it says: "Decisions of the Crisis Staff shall be binding for all the crisis staffs in the municipalities." This is the Official Gazette of the ARK and the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff, signed by Radoslav Brdjanin. It says here: "These decisions of the Crisis Staff shall be submitted to the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina for their verification as soon as it is able to convene." Item 6: "An agency shall be established immediately that will work on the problem of population resettlement." Is that what you meant? Were you referring to agencies of this kind when you said that we oversaw the -- or, rather, that the crisis staffs oversaw the removal of non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see in a great many municipalities is an institution named, variously, Property -- exchange Agency, or Agency for Movement of Population, or so on. It is established at the ARK level, but also at the municipal level, and these agencies were often named by the crisis staffs and war presidencies as the institutions through which the moving out of the population was to be organised, including the signing over of property. So I don't mean simply this ARK one. I also see them in many individual municipalities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will get back to this issue of property being signed over. This is what you're reading into this, but this was not done, this was not implemented. You don't know that, but this was not implemented. Can this please be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did we see in this document, Mr. Karadzic? What answer did we hear from the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in this -- well, it was an evasive answer. The answer was supposed to be -- did you mean agencies described in Article 6 here: "An agency shall be established that will work on the problem of population resettlement"? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see agencies like that formed in many municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 795 [Realtime transcript read in error "785"]? The previous one was dated the 26th of May, and this one. The transcript says "785." It should be "795." We see the right document, but the transcript is incorrect. It says "785." It should read "795."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that this is actually six days before the document speaking about the formation of the agency. The date is the 20th of May. "Conclusions": "First of all, there is no reason for the population of any ethnic background to move out of the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." Were you aware of the fact that this was the position taken by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I'm aware we've had many trials -- we've had trials on the Crisis Staff in Autonomous Region of Krajina precisely on the question of the removal of the population -- non-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you see that the decision on the establishment of the agency was actually taken one week after the position was adopted? Does this not tell you that this was something that was inevitable, and that even after this conclusion, requests were made by people who wanted to move out?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is this something that was inevitable; the creation of agencies? I'm just not clear on your question. What was inevitable?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, Madam, whether you know that the initial position taken by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina was that there was no reason for people to move out, and yet a week later they had to establish an agency that would regulate that process.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that they had to establish an agency. They chose to. As for whether their -- what their public announcement was, that there was no reason for people to move out, as I said, we know and we've established for the trial that they did intend people to move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you include this position by this Crisis Staff in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be received, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to look at 65 ter 398. We are going back to Kotor Varos, the striking example -- a municipality that is a striking example, representative of everything, according to your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a bulletin published by the War Presidency of the Municipality of Kotor Varos. The date is the 24th of July, 1992. And we can move on to page 2 both in the Serbian and in the English versions. The third paragraph says: "The extremists from Vecici constantly harass the people of neighbouring villages, so that the people of the hamlet of Vasiljevici left the village and found shelter with their relatives in Vrbanjci. "The extremists from Bilice have, over the past few days, opened fire on Plana. A few days ago, they treacherously killed Ranko Vucanovic while he was mowing a field, after which they set fire to the houses and cattle-sheds belonging to Djordje Djuric and Slavko Zaric. Extremists from Vecici co-operate with the fundamentalists from Ravne and Kotor, who set fire to the house of livestock breeder Andjelko Popovic in Zubovici. Extremists spread fear among the people in the rest of Serbian villages as well, forcing them to seek safety in other villages." And then it goes on to say: "The frequent attacks by extremists on Serbian settlements indicate that there is a need to take more vigorous action in mopping up the municipality's terrain and disarming the extremists in order to bring back peace to the entire area." Were you aware of the fact that in late July, there was this terror campaign against Serb villages in the municipality of Kotor Varos, and is this something that you've taken into consideration and included in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this bulletin. I see many references to extremists and fundamentalists as the enemy -- the Serbs describe the enemy as extremists and fundamentalists. So I've read this bulletin, so I certainly saw this passage. No, I did not include it in my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next page, please, in both English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here in the third paragraph: "The War Presidency analysed information regarding appropriation of abandoned property from houses and other buildings, and, in order to prevent such conduct by individuals, ordered strengthened checks of entry and exit at all check-points in order to detect and put on record individuals who are taking advantage of the war situation in order to try to profit from it. In contacts with the army command, their attention was drawn to this, that they should do everything possible to preserve and protect all property and prevent its unnecessary wanton destruction." Did you know that the War Presidency was taking such efforts, and did you include this in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would note an error there in the translation. It's not "preserve and protect," it's "preserve and use all property." The written text is correct, but the simultaneous translation was wrong. So, in fact, the army commands are being told to do everything possible to preserve and use all property. I was aware of the efforts to control property, put it to the use of the municipality. I did not include this specific reference in my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Page 4, please, in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "List of deserted houses and flats. "One development that should be noted is the abandoning of flats by extremists and other Muslims and Croats ..." Do you see, Ms. Hanson, that a distinction is being made between extremists and other Muslims and Croats? You said a moment ago that we called our enemy "fundamentalists." Do you see that a distinction here is made between citizens and extremists?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, the distinction is made, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. "So that as of today, some socially-owned flats have been abandoned, and some family houses, socially-owned flats, are those that people used temporarily because they have occupancy rights." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. "In view of the fact that Croatian and Muslim families are being resettled, those who wanted, it is to be expected that we will have a large abandoned" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic is kindly asked to read more slowly and give us a reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Interpreters were not able to catch up with you. Could you repeat, and read slow, and reference as well?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the last paragraph: "The list of deserted houses and flats ..." "The War Presidency and Municipal Secretariat for Urban Planning and Construction have done what was in their power; that is to say, they have registered and sealed flats and houses, with people on duty in blocks of flats ..." Et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't this protection of this property?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next page. The English page can remain briefly, but we need the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "However, some flats have been broken into, and the Public Security Station in Kotor Varos has received an express order from the War Presidency to take all perpetrators of such acts into custody, and we must persevere in this task, so that we expect unselfish assistance from citizens and relevant CZ officials in discovering and reporting perpetrators of these and similar acts. "The owners of the abandoned flats grant temporary use of these flats, through the Municipal Civil Protection Staff, to the workers whose houses or flats had been destroyed in war." Do you see that this is temporary use?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here they say "temporary use."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 6 -- page 5 first in English and page 6 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Resettling the population." It says: "The pernicious policy of Muslim and Croatian extremists is increasingly losing supporters even among other Muslims and Croats. The population, which they had led astray and then let down, is increasingly and openly turning their backs on them. Many reasonable people, including a group of Muslim intellectuals, realising the full absurdity of resisting the Serbian Army and new authorities ..." You can all read for yourselves. Next page, please. It says: "The population, misled by empty promises, is seeking help from the Serbian municipality ..." And then it says: "A considerable number of Muslims and Croats --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please read more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat. Again, the interpreters were not able to catch up with your speed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have to read every word. We have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This paragraph explains that a considerable number of Croats and Muslims are feeling the uncertainty and want to move to other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina or to join their families abroad. I will read: "The War Presidency and other relevant organs, showing great understanding for these unfortunate people, and acting in accordance with the existing laws and regulations of the Serbian Republic of BH, the region and municipality, has begun resettling the population in an organised manner. This activity is proceeding in accordance with the wishes expressed by these population groups. To this end, transportation and appropriate protection have been provided ..." And it says further down that: "Three convoys have so far been organised and escorted." Do you see that this is about securing and escorting convoys and meeting the requests of those people?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cite this in my report, I believe. The municipality is organising the transport. They're acting in accordance with the laws of the Serbian BH in the region, and they're moving out the population in accordance with their understanding of the population's wishes. They are not trying to create conditions of security for the people in the municipality. They're not trying to move them to another part of the municipality which is safe. They're moving them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how did you come to that conclusion? From where does that follow? Isn't it clear from this that citizens are requesting this, it's their wish? It's not that the municipality's interpreting or misinterpreting their wishes. Where will we see an end to your insinuations?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a general understanding of the events throughout Bosnia, and I believe the Court will hear or has heard witnesses who say that they were not leaving entirely voluntarily. I do not -- I haven't followed the trial of this, I don't know what the witnesses have said, but I know from other trials that the general atmosphere there was such that people said they wanted to leave because the other -- the only other option they felt was death or detention; was unbearable circumstances. I do not see the municipality here trying to simply move them to another part of the municipality. We saw that with people on the front-line, we saw in an earlier document, being moved within the municipality to a safer place. Here, they don't seem to be offered that. They are saying they want to leave, according to the War Presidency. That's why I say that conclusion, that it's the War Presidency saying these people want to leave. I do not always -- cannot take that simply on face value, given the events in this and other municipalities. And, moreover, we see Kotor Varos later making sure that people who left do not come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you make your report based on documentation or based on rumours and the testimony of other witnesses in other trials? What was the subject of your work? What was the material you used?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not base -- I did not use any rumours, nor any witness testimony in my report. It was on documentation, based on documentation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then let's stick to the documentation on which your report is based. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1310, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 397, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session from the 26th of July of the same War Presidency. Let's look at the last bullet point in item 2, where it says that: "For today's meeting of the War Presidency, reports should be prepared on the resettlement of population ..." The next page in English. "... resettlement of population, the harvest, humanitarian aid, the operation to seal flats and houses, and protection of abandoned property, the dead and the wounded, and reports on the take-over of goods from shops." Did you have this document in mind, and do you see what the War Presidency is doing?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Presidency is seeking reports on the resettlement of population and other important things in the municipality, such as goods -- resources, the harvest, and goods, and protection of -- the sealing of property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the protection of property; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1311, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 246, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session of the same Presidency, 28th of July, 1992. Look at item 2: "As part of this item, members of the War Presidency reported on their activities for the past day. In relation to the report of the chief of the SJB on confiscating the money of individuals who are moving out, it was established that this was being done without anyone's orders; that is, in an unauthorised manner, and this can have a negative effect on the operation and the reputation of all of us ..." Et cetera. And then an order was given to Vrbanjci Agricultural Co-operative to open up a shop in Vrbanjci. Vrbanjci is not a Serb village, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Vrbanjci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the last paragraph in item 2? The Executive Board -- the Executive Committee will begin to work. It is their judgement that the Executive Committee can start operating like in normal times?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All you asked about this document is about Vrbanjci; was that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have a further comment on the first paragraph, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he notes, yes, that the money -- that money has been confiscated from individuals moving out, apparently without authorisation, but the money that is so confiscated will be used to help families of soldiers killed and other essential costs of the municipality. It is not being held temporarily and securely for those who will return. The money taken from people moving out is to be used by the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1312, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When will they return, Ms. Hanson? When will they return? That money is being used temporarily, because the municipality has the legal right to use all the material resources. Instead of keeping it in their treasury, they are using it for humanitarian purposes; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Instead of keeping it in the treasury, they're using it, yes. And they say essential costs of the municipality, not necessarily humanitarian ones. But it's interesting that they claim it was done without anybody's order, in an unauthorised manner, and yet the municipality is able to take that money. They clearly have it. So the question is: Who's been doing the confiscating and how the War Presidency, in this case, can actually use the money? If it's been individuals out of control, how can the War Presidency hold that money?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we'll see. 65 ter 264, please, 264.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here is what is being said the next day on the issue I'm asking you about.
